lm_output:
"In yonder groves the happy souls reside,
And in those shades we live, and lie on mossy beds,
By crystal streams, that murmur thro' the meads:
But pass yon easy hill, and thence descend;
The path conducts you to your journey's end."

This said, he led the way, and soon they reached
The hermit's cell, where Vellaisamy preached
To numerous pupils, who around him sate
In circles on the ground, and listened to his lecture.

The judge, who well the human heart could judge
By every tell-tale sign, and who could read
The most inexplicable passion in the eyes
And on the cheek, beheld with joy
The pure and unmistakable expression
That love, uncalled, unbounded, and unbiased,
Had stamped upon the features of Gayatri,
And of Vellaisamy, who, conscious of his passion,
Avoided her regard, and dared not meet
Her eye, which, though it modestly was lowered,
Yet spoke the feelings of her heart so loud,
That, had it not been heard, it must have been
Because the judge was deaf. He saw, he knew,
Their love was innocent, and therefore trusted it.
He saw, he knew, their hearts were pure and spotless,
And therefore gave them to each other, as
A victim to the God of Love, to be
Immolated on his altar. Soon the day
Of their espousals came; and, when the rites
Of marriage were performed, the hermit led
The bride and bridegroom to the nuptial bed,
And blessed them, as he left them to enjoy
Their new-made joys, in peace, and in tranquility."
